Subject: Performance SLO & Regional Routing - Post-call recap

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and can propose a short PoC plan: 

Key outcomes from the call:
- Primary use case: low-latency conversational routing for customer support (embedding + streaming generation).
- Expected peak throughput: ~1,200 requests/minute (spiky), baseline ~400 requests/min.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end generation time <= 300ms for short responses (<=128 tokens); soft target <= 200ms for streaming-first-token.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~250, bursts up to 600.
- Streaming: client expects token-by-token streaming (websocket or SSE) with first-token within 150-200ms for US traffic.
- Regional requirements: US and EU traffic must be served from local regions. APAC is lower priority but should be routed to Singapore/Tokyo region with relaxed SLOs.
- Data residency: EU customer PII must remain in EU region. You noted some PCI-adjacent fields in transcripts that need to be redacted at rest.

Open/clarifying items we agreed to validate:
1) Confirm whether the 300ms p95 includes network transit from the user to the region (Tom: you indicated yes; we'll assume app front-end to region is included).
2) Exact success criteria for the PoC (throughput+latency targets, example prompt set).
3) Any compliance artifacts required for EU residency (KMS, audit logs).
4) Please confirm required retention windows.

Next steps (proposed):
- We'll share a short SLO workbook (attached) that maps your traffic profile to expected throughput, batching, and cost estimates.
- Aditya will reply with technical notes on batching, KV cache warmup, and multi-region routing options.
- Marissa to schedule a 30-min tech demo + PoC kickoff once we have agreed success criteria.

Attachments: finova_slo_requirements.xlsx (SLO workbook), redwood_multi-region-arch.png (high-level routing diagram)

Thanks — feel free to correct anything I've misstated.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@finova.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:45 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Regional Routing - Post-call recap

Marissa — thanks for the write-up, this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 300ms p95 includes client-to-region transit. Our users are mostly on mobile across US/EU.
- For the PoC success criteria: aim for p95 <= 300ms for US region at 500 concurrent users (sustained for 10 min), and p95 <= 350ms for EU at 200 concurrent users. APAC: p95 <= 500ms, optional for initial PoC.
- Streaming: first-token within 200ms is important for perceived responsiveness. We'll accept slightly higher end-to-end if first-token is timely.
- Data residency: EU transcripts containing PII must be stored and processed in EU. We can provide the list of fields that must be redacted at rest; retention window is 7 years for audit. We also need proof of customer-managed KMS or HSM access for EU-hosted keys.

One question for your engineering team: how do you guarantee routing by region for API-level customers? We need to avoid any EU traffic touching non-EU hosting for both inference and cache hot paths.

I can confirm the PoC success criteria above if Redwood can commit to a short trial where we run a simulated load from our APAC, EU, and US agents.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Product, Finova

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:34:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Regional Routing - Post-call recap

Hi Tom — copying Lauren for routing/ops details. Quick technical responses to the items you raised: 

1) Regional routing and data residency:
- Redwood can route at the customer or route-level based on the source IP or an explicit region header. For your setup we recommend configuring per-tenant routing + a geo-failover policy. That ensures EU-labeled requests never leave EU-hosted inference pools.
- KV cache and prefix cache can be pinned per-region; we'll ensure cache keys for EU tenants live in EU region only. For long-term persistence we support customer-managed KMS in EU (we'll need an IAM/KMS setup during PoC).

2) Latency guarantees and streaming:
- Streaming first-token timings depend on model choice and prompt size. For small prompts (<=128 tokens) we expect first-token 80-160ms on modern GPUs in our hosted fleet with optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for streaming routes.
- The 300ms p95 target is achievable in US/EU with tuned batch sizes (we recommend batch cap of 16 for interactive routes) and a small model variant for latency-critical paths. For APAC we recommend colocating inference in Singapore/Tokyo and using a slightly larger p95 target (as Tom suggested).

3) Throughput & concurrency:
- Given your peak of 1,200 req/min, concurrency 600, and expected token lengths, our initial calc (see attached workbook) suggests a baseline of 4 dedicated concurrent inference workers in each region with autoscale to 12 under sustained spikes. This assumes efficient batching and 16-token average generation.
- During PoC we can run a controlled load test with your synthetic traffic to validate autoscaling thresholds and cold-start behavior.

4) Failover and graceful degradation:
- We can configure fallback model variants and region fallback policies (e.g., EU->EU secondary, then EU->US only under explicit emergency approvals) so that production traffic will not fail open to non-EU by default. Any cross-region failover that would move EU PII will be blocked unless explicitly approved in the console.

Attachments: finova_slo_requirements.xlsx (updated tab with region-specific worker counts), redwood_multi-region-arch.png

Happy to sync over a short tech demo to run through the PoC plan and the KMS handshake steps.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
